Furthermore, the landmark case of Ali v. Ashcroft, 476 F.3d 568 (9th Cir. 2007), established that asylum seekers can rely on the totality of the circumstances, including employment-related disruptions, to establish a well-founded fear of persecution. This precedent directly supports the claim that private employer conduct, such as withdrawal of sponsorship, can be considered in asylum proceedings.

(See also, 8 U.S.C. § 1158(a)(2)(A)).
